question: In which year was the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) established?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1920**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was established on **31 October 1920** in Bombay (now Mumbai), India.
 
• Prominent leaders such as **Lala Lajpat Rai**, Joseph Baptista, N.M. Joshi, and Diwan Chaman Lall were instrumental in its foundation.
 
• AITUC was the **first national-level trade union organization in India**, created to represent and protect the rights of workers.
 
• The first president of AITUC was **Lala Lajpat Rai**, a noted freedom fighter and social reformer.
 
• The organization played a critical role in the **Indian freedom struggle** by organizing workers and opposing exploitation under colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Trade Union Congress (INTUC)**

 
 
• Affiliation: Indian National Congress (INC).
 
• Focus: Gandhian principles, harmonious relations, large membership in textiles, mining.
 
• Key: Largest union by membership, aims for social security and welfare.** **
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS)**
 
 
• Affiliation: Bhartiya Jan Sangh/BJP (RSS-linked).
 
• Focus: Nationalist ideology, strong growth, focusing on worker welfare, often seen as a counter to left unions.
 
• Key: Often third largest, gaining ground in recent years. 
 
 
 
• **Hind Mazdoor Sangh (HMS)**
 
 
• Affiliation: Socialist parties (Praja Socialist, Samyukta Socialist).
 
• Focus: Keeping free from major political interference, strong in Railways, Textiles, Engineering.
 
• Key: Formed by socialists who wanted independence from INTUC/AITUC. 
 
 
 
• **Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU)**
 
 
• Affiliation: Communist Party of India (Marxist) - CPI(M).
 
• Focus: Militant struggle for higher wages, social security, resisting privatization.
 
• Key: Strong in West Bengal, Kerala, Tripura; left-wing alternative to AITUC.
